evals.prompt: Synthesize unreleased feature commits across multiple repos into a comprehensive Canonical Foundation Narrative (CANONICAL.md) before cutting platform posts.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive, unconstrained single source of truth document detailing project context, verified commit details, performance observations, architectural rationale, and verified links.
assertions: The canonical document details exact changes per repository without relying on one-line commit summaries
Documents real architectural failure modes, trade-offs, and philosophies
Acts as the unconstrained master source from which all platform-specific cuts derive
Includes exact repository URLs and verified links

evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing an open-source Go tool that reduces PostgreSQL query latency by 40% using lock-free buffer pooling. Include benchmarks and discuss trade-offs.
evals.expected_output: High-performing LinkedIn technical case study formatted with strong mobile hook (<140 chars), concrete metrics, trade-offs, link in first comment guidance, and 1-3 targeted hashtags.
assertions: The first line delivers a concrete technical metric or hook within 140 characters before the fold
The copy explicitly explains the architectural mechanism (lock-free buffer pooling)
The copy explicitly addresses technical trade-offs or constraints
External links are directed to the first comment rather than placed in the post body
The post contains between 1 and 3 domain-specific hashtags at the end
The text contains no banned AI slop words (e.g., 'delve', 'game-changer', 'revolutionary')

evals.prompt: Draft an X / Twitter native long-form post covering a weekend architectural overhaul across multiple tools, explaining why the team moved from rigid hooks to educative skills.
evals.expected_output: A native long-form post with an above-the-fold hook (<240 chars), bulleted changelog, architectural lesson, direct project links, and 0 hashtags.
assertions: The opening hook is under 280 characters before the 'Show more' fold
The post delivers substantive native context and high dwell-time value
Contains 0 hashtags
Includes direct links to the relevant repositories/articles directly at the bottom

evals.prompt: Write a multi-post Bluesky thread breaking down a major open-source release across 5 repositories and explaining the core architectural lesson.
evals.expected_output: A multi-post thread where every single post is strictly under 300 graphemes, featuring authentic developer tone, direct links with rich cards, and 0-1 hashtags.
assertions: Every single post in the thread is strictly 300 graphemes or less
External links are placed directly in the relevant post bodies
Uses authentic, anti-corporate developer tone with zero AI buzzwords
Contains at most 1 specific hashtag across the thread

evals.prompt: Create an Instagram 7-slide carousel outline and micro-blog caption teaching junior engineers how to avoid N+1 database queries.
evals.expected_output: A 7-slide 4:5 carousel outline with visual/copy breakdown and a micro-blog caption with a <125-char hook and comment-to-DM CTA.
assertions: Specifies 4:5 vertical aspect ratio for slides
Contains a slide-by-slide outline (Cover, Anti-pattern, Refactor, Benchmark, Architecture, Cheat sheet, CTA)
The caption hook is under 125 characters before the fold
Includes a single-word comment automation CTA (e.g., comment keyword for guide)
Includes 3 to 5 targeted hashtags at the footer

evals.prompt: Draft a Reddit self-post for r/golang sharing an open-source zero-allocation JSON parser with benchmarks against the standard library.
evals.expected_output: A value-first text post with a non-clickbait title, benchmark markdown table, architecture explanation, limitations, and transparent affiliation.
assertions: The title is descriptive, technical, and non-clickbait
The post body provides 100% of the architectural insights and benchmarks directly on Reddit
Includes a Markdown benchmark table comparing throughput and memory allocations
Explicitly documents current limitations and trade-offs
Includes transparent author affiliation disclosure and places external repo link at the bottom

evals.prompt: Write a Threads post discussing why a team replaced microservices with a modular monolith, sharing the latency results and asking for peer experiences.
evals.expected_output: A 500-character builder post with concrete latency delta, open-ended discussion question, and exactly 1 natural language topic tag.
assertions: The post is under 500 characters
Contains concrete latency or architectural metrics
Ends with an open-ended technical question encouraging peer discussion
Uses exactly one natural-language topic tag (e.g., #system design)
